blocks.body: # AI-enabled scientific discoveries: audited seed census

**Evidence cut-off: 2 August 2026.** This is a high-confidence, cross-science seed catalog—not a claim to have found every AI-enabled discovery ever made. No exhaustive global index exists, and the meaning of both *AI* and *discovery* varies by field.

## Executive summary

The audit found **25 source-backed study-level cases across eight discipline groups**. Twenty-two have case-appropriate empirical or observational corroboration (Tier A); three are published computational or statistical results with partial validation (Tier B). The strongest pattern is not autonomous science: in nearly every case, AI searched or generated at scale while researchers framed the problem, ran instruments or experiments, verified candidates, and interpreted the result.

- **AI has contributed to genuine discoveries**, including planets and radio bursts, field-verified geoglyphs, a new fossil species, hidden earthquake populations, experimentally tested materials and drug candidates, and new biological or neural patterns.
- **Evidence stage matters more than the word ‘discovered’.** A field-verified geoglyph, a mouse-tested antibiotic, a phase 2a drug candidate, and a predicted stable crystal do not carry the same evidential weight.
- **Large headline totals are usually candidate or mapping counts.** The ledger does not add 109,956 craters, 381,000 predicted crystals, and one clinical candidate into a meaningless grand total.
- **Human–AI attribution is inseparable.** Even the most autonomous workflow here relied on human-built instruments, datasets, objectives, safeguards, and later scientific interpretation.
- **Biomedical science dominates this seed audit (11 of 25 cases).** That reflects both a dense experimental literature and this first-pass search, not proof that AI is scientifically more productive there than everywhere else.

## The reviewed cases

Use the exact result and caveat columns together. Tier A means direct corroboration appropriate to the case; it does not mean clinical approval, independent replication, or final scientific truth.

## Selected primary evidence

- [Kepler neural-network planet search](https://science.nasa.gov/universe/exoplanets/discovery-of-eight-planets-makes-alien-system-the-first-to-tie-with-our-solar-system/)
- [AI-accelerated Nazca survey](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2407652121)
- [Oldest sepioid found through zero-shot fossil mining](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42003-026-09519-9)
- [GNoME material-stability atlas](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06735-9)
- [Generative de novo antibiotics](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2025.07.033)
- [Co-Scientist biomedical validations](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10644-y)
- [East Antarctic upper-mantle earthquakes](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aea9895)
- [Sperm-whale coda structure](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-47221-8)

## What was deliberately not counted

A credible registry needs a visible negative space. These influential examples are useful, but treating all of them as first discoveries would collapse the distinction between prediction, validation, rediscovery, capability, and empirical novelty.

## Coverage is incomplete by design

This first sweep is strongest in biomedicine and remains incomplete in physics, climate and ocean science, botany, agriculture, and several biological subfields. A zero below records an audit gap—not an assertion that no discovery exists.

## Recommended registry design

1. Add a domain-neutral science schema in a new migration; do not rewrite the mathematics history.
2. Make evidence stage, validation tier, novelty class, AI role, human role, source date, and caveat first-class fields.
3. Keep separate views for first discovery, human–AI co-discovery, rediscovery, validation, prediction, and capability demonstration.
4. Require a primary source and retain corrections, replications, retractions, and priority disputes as versioned updates.
5. Publish the coverage ledger beside the catalog so ‘all’ is always an auditable goal rather than a marketing claim.

## Questions before product integration

- Should the registry include theoretical and computational discoveries before physical validation?
- Should social and behavioural sciences be in scope, or should the first expansion stay with natural science and archaeology?
- Which fields require a subject-matter reviewer before publication?
- What update cadence and correction policy will keep 2026-era claims current?

## Required caveat

**Share with caveats.** This is a source-backed starting census, not a systematic review or a proof of completeness. Publication bias, terminology drift, heterogeneous evidence, contested novelty, and future corrections remain material. Counts describe reviewed cases only and must not be presented as the total scientific output of AI.

## Method and files

The full definitions, source procedure, tier rules, limitations, chart contract, and expansion requirements are in `METHODOLOGY.md`. The portable report is generated from the same bounded datasets in `artifact.json`; `discoveries.csv`, `exclusions.csv`, and `coverage_ledger.csv` remain the inspectable ledgers.

discoveries.title: Kepler-90i and Kepler-80g
discoveries.ai_role: A neural network ranked weak transit-like signals in archival Kepler data.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers selected training data, inspected the signals, and performed astronomical and statistical validation.
discoveries.novelty_scope: previously missed celestial objects
discoveries.reported_result: Two previously missed planets were found; Kepler-90 became the first known eight-planet system outside the Solar System.
discoveries.caveat: The AI did not observe the sky autonomously; it re-analysed archival signals and the discovery still depended on human validation.

discoveries.title: Seventy-two additional bursts from FRB 121102
discoveries.ai_role: A convolutional neural network searched a five-hour radio dataset for burst morphology.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers dedispersed and inspected the returned events and interpreted the burst timing.
discoveries.evidence_stage: observed signals verified in archival telescope data
discoveries.novelty_scope: new events from a known source
discoveries.reported_result: The model recovered 72 bursts missed by the conventional search, raising the dataset total from 21 to 93.
discoveries.caveat: This was archival re-analysis of a known repeating fast-radio-burst source, not discovery of a new source.

discoveries.title: SN 2023tyk end-to-end autonomous transient discovery workflow
discoveries.ai_role: BTSbot classified a transient candidate, triggered robotic spectroscopy, classified the spectrum, and submitted the result without human intervention.
discoveries.human_role: Humans designed the pipeline, operated the surveys and instruments, and audited the resulting record.
discoveries.evidence_stage: observed, spectroscopically classified, and publicly reported
discoveries.novelty_scope: new astronomical transient plus autonomous workflow milestone
discoveries.reported_result: SN 2023tyk was the first reported transient to complete the discovery-to-classification-to-public-report chain without human action.
discoveries.caveat: The scientific object was detected by survey infrastructure; the novelty is the AI-orchestrated end-to-end workflow, not autonomous physical interpretation.

discoveries.title: 109,956 previously unrecognized lunar craters
discoveries.ai_role: A transfer-learning system detected craters and estimated geologic ages from Chang'E imagery and elevation data.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers curated training data, assessed error and recovery rates, and interpreted crater chronology.
discoveries.evidence_stage: peer-reviewed computational mapping with benchmark validation
discoveries.novelty_scope: previously uncatalogued planetary surface features
discoveries.reported_result: The study reported 109,956 new craters and estimated formation systems for 18,996 craters larger than 8 km.
discoveries.caveat: Most entries are model-detected map features rather than individually field-verified objects; age assignments are model estimates.

discoveries.title: Upper-mantle earthquakes beneath East Antarctica
discoveries.ai_role: Deep learning with transfer learning detected small seismic events across 49 stations.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers visually checked waveforms, located events, and interpreted the tectonic mechanism.
discoveries.evidence_stage: observational catalog with manual waveform checks
discoveries.novelty_scope: previously unknown earthquake population and process evidence
discoveries.reported_result: The catalog contained 1,068 events beneath David Glacier, including 510 intermediate-depth earthquakes at roughly 100-150 km, revealing unexpected intraplate seismicity.
discoveries.caveat: The physical interpretation remains a scientific inference from the newly detected catalog, not a direct measurement of mantle mechanism.

discoveries.title: 303 new figurative Nazca geoglyphs
discoveries.ai_role: A deep-learning model prioritized likely geoglyph locations in aerial imagery.
discoveries.human_role: Archaeologists inspected candidates on the ground and interpreted style, distribution, and use.
discoveries.novelty_scope: previously undocumented archaeological objects
discoveries.reported_result: An AI-accelerated six-month survey found 303 new figurative relief-type geoglyphs, nearly doubling the known count of that class and increasing the discovery rate about sixteen-fold.
discoveries.caveat: AI prioritized survey targets; humans made the archaeological confirmation and interpretation.

discoveries.title: Uluciala rotundata, the oldest known sepioid
discoveries.ai_role: A zero-shot segmentation model isolated fossils from full-colour grinding-tomography image stacks without taxon-specific training.
discoveries.human_role: Paleontologists reconstructed, described, deposited, and taxonomically interpreted the fossils.
discoveries.evidence_stage: physical specimens, peer-reviewed taxonomy, and open 3D models
discoveries.novelty_scope: new genus and species plus earliest fossil record
discoveries.reported_result: Two approximately 74-67 million-year-old beaks defined Uluciala rotundata and provided intermediate morphology between cuttlefish and bobtail squid lineages.
discoveries.caveat: The AI segmented candidate fossils; the species diagnosis and evolutionary conclusion were human scientific work.

discoveries.title: Sixfold-improved photocatalyst formulation found by a mobile robotic chemist
discoveries.ai_role: Bayesian search selected experiments for a mobile robot across a ten-variable formulation space.
discoveries.human_role: Chemists defined the objective, reagents and apparatus and interpreted the optimized mixture.
discoveries.novelty_scope: new high-performing formulation
discoveries.reported_result: The autonomous campaign found a photocatalyst mixture with activity about six times higher than the initial formulations.
discoveries.caveat: This is discovery of an optimized mixture under a specified assay, not a new fundamental catalytic law or necessarily a new molecule.

discoveries.title: GNoME stable-material candidate atlas
discoveries.ai_role: Graph networks predicted stability across a very large inorganic crystal search space.
discoveries.human_role: Materials scientists constructed the training corpus, recalculated stability, compared against experiments, and assessed limitations.
discoveries.evidence_stage: published computational atlas with partial experimental matches
discoveries.novelty_scope: new predicted crystal structures
discoveries.reported_result: The study reported 2.2 million stable structures, 381,000 on the updated convex hull, 45,500 new prototypes, and 736 matches to independently synthesized structures.
discoveries.caveat: The headline structures are predictions, not 381,000 synthesized materials; stability can change with better calculations and says little by itself about synthesizability or useful properties.

discoveries.title: MatterGen target-conditioned inorganic material
discoveries.ai_role: A diffusion model generated crystal structures conditioned on target properties.
discoveries.human_role: Scientists selected a candidate, synthesized it, characterized it, and compared the measured property with the design target.
discoveries.novelty_scope: new AI-designed material candidate
discoveries.reported_result: A generated material was synthesized as a proof of concept and its measured target property was within about 20% of the requested value.
discoveries.caveat: One proof-of-concept synthesis does not experimentally validate the much larger generated candidate space or establish manufacturability.

discoveries.title: Halicin as a broad-spectrum antibacterial
discoveries.ai_role: A deep neural network learned antibacterial activity and screened a repurposing library plus more than ten million purchasable molecules.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers tested hits, named halicin, studied mechanism, and ran animal infection experiments.
discoveries.novelty_scope: new antibacterial function for an existing molecule
discoveries.reported_result: Halicin showed broad bactericidal activity and efficacy in mouse models of Clostridioides difficile and pan-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii; eight additional antibacterial hits emerged from 23 tested predictions.
discoveries.caveat: Halicin was an existing molecule repurposed for a newly identified function; it remains preclinical and is not an approved antibiotic.

discoveries.title: Abaucin, a narrow-spectrum Acinetobacter baumannii antibiotic
discoveries.ai_role: A neural network trained on roughly 7,500 screened compounds prioritized structurally distinct molecules.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers performed susceptibility, resistance, genetic, mechanistic, and mouse-wound experiments.
discoveries.evidence_stage: in vitro, mechanism studies, and mouse model
discoveries.novelty_scope: new antibacterial candidate and target pathway
discoveries.reported_result: Abaucin selectively inhibited A. baumannii, implicated LolE-dependent lipoprotein trafficking, and reduced bacterial burden in a mouse wound model.
discoveries.caveat: This is a preclinical lead, not a medicine proven safe or effective in humans.

discoveries.title: Explainable-AI antibiotic class active against MRSA and VRE
discoveries.ai_role: Graph neural networks plus explainability filters screened more than twelve million compounds for predicted activity and low human-cell toxicity.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers tested 283 compounds, analysed structure and resistance, and ran mouse infection models.
discoveries.evidence_stage: in vitro, resistance studies, and mouse models
discoveries.novelty_scope: new structural class of antibacterial candidates
discoveries.reported_result: The study identified a structurally distinct class active against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and vancomycin-resistant enterococci, with low resistance frequency and reduced bacterial titres in mouse models.
discoveries.caveat: The compounds are preclinical; explainability highlighted learned substructures but did not make the model or biological mechanism fully understood.

discoveries.title: BRD-K56819078 as a senolytic lead
discoveries.ai_role: A graph neural network trained on a 2,352-compound senolytic screen ranked more than 800,000 molecules.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers tested prioritized compounds in cells and evaluated a lead in aged mice.
discoveries.novelty_scope: new senolytic candidate
discoveries.reported_result: Three drug-like senolytic candidates were validated; BRD-K56819078 reduced senescent-cell burden and senescence-associated gene expression in aged mouse kidneys.
discoveries.caveat: Mouse and cell results do not establish rejuvenation, lifespan extension, safety, or efficacy in people.

discoveries.title: Antibiotic candidates reconstructed from extinct proteomes
discoveries.discovery_class: candidate discovery from ancient sequence space
discoveries.ai_role: APEX machine-learning models mined 10,311,899 ancient protein sequences and prioritized encrypted antimicrobial peptides.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers synthesized 69 candidates and performed microbiology and mouse infection experiments.
discoveries.novelty_scope: previously unknown peptide antibiotics from extinct organisms
discoveries.reported_result: The system predicted 37,176 broad-spectrum candidates, including 11,035 absent from living organisms; multiple synthesized leads were active in mouse infection models.
discoveries.caveat: Most predicted peptides were not synthesized, and the validated leads remain preclinical.

discoveries.title: NG1 and DN1 de novo antibiotics
discoveries.ai_role: Generative deep-learning systems searched more than ten million fragment combinations and designed chemically novel compounds.
discoveries.human_role: Chemists synthesized 24 candidates; biologists tested activity, selectivity, mechanism, resistance, and mouse infection models.
discoveries.novelty_scope: de novo antibiotic structures and distinct mechanisms
discoveries.reported_result: Seven of 24 synthesized designs were selectively active; NG1 and DN1 reduced bacterial burden in mouse gonorrhoea and MRSA skin-infection models and acted through distinct mechanisms.
discoveries.caveat: These are early preclinical leads, not approved drugs; only a tiny fraction of the generated chemical space was synthesized.

discoveries.title: TNIK and rentosertib for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
discoveries.ai_role: Generative AI contributed to identifying TNIK as a fibrosis target and designing the small-molecule inhibitor rentosertib.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers performed preclinical studies and a 71-participant randomized phase 2a trial.
discoveries.novelty_scope: new therapeutic target and AI-designed clinical candidate
discoveries.reported_result: Over 12 weeks, the 60 mg once-daily arm showed a mean FVC change of +98.4 ml versus -20.3 ml for placebo, while the study primarily assessed safety and tolerability.
discoveries.caveat: The trial was small and short, FVC was secondary, 16 of 71 participants withdrew, liver-related toxicity caused several discontinuations, and efficacy is not established.

discoveries.title: MP20 and A1 against multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae
discoveries.ai_role: A graph neural network trained on 38,650 measured molecules virtually screened about six million compounds.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers tested 213 predictions, investigated mechanism, and used a human vagina-on-a-chip and mouse infection model.
discoveries.evidence_stage: in vitro, organ-on-chip, and mouse model
discoveries.novelty_scope: new selective antibacterial candidates and mechanism
discoveries.reported_result: Eighty-three of 213 tested predictions inhibited N. gonorrhoeae; MP20 and A1 were structurally unlike existing antibiotics, and A1 was shown to target alanine racemase.
discoveries.caveat: These are preclinical candidates and have not been shown safe or effective in human patients.

discoveries.title: Co-Scientist acute myeloid leukaemia candidates
discoveries.ai_role: A multi-agent Gemini system searched and critiqued drug-repurposing and combination hypotheses under expert constraints.
discoveries.human_role: Oncologists curated proposals and researchers performed independent dose-response experiments in cancer and control cell lines.
discoveries.novelty_scope: new indication hypotheses and combinations
discoveries.reported_result: The system proposed active AML candidates and combinations; KIRA6 showed selective cytotoxicity with an approximately eighteen-fold separation between KG-1a AML and TK6 control cells.
discoveries.caveat: Cell-line activity is preliminary; several hits had prior rationale, and none of the reported AML uses or combinations is clinically validated.

discoveries.title: Co-Scientist epigenetic targets and repurposing hypotheses for liver fibrosis
discoveries.ai_role: A multi-agent system generated and ranked epigenetic target hypotheses and matching drugs.
discoveries.human_role: Experts selected three hypotheses and researchers tested them in human hepatic organoids with live-cell imaging.
discoveries.novelty_scope: new target hypotheses and repurposed candidate uses
discoveries.reported_result: Two of three selected target-drug hypotheses showed significant anti-fibrotic activity without detected cellular toxicity; one effective drug was vorinostat.
discoveries.caveat: Organoid results are not evidence of safety or efficacy in patients; one candidate is approved for a different indication only.

discoveries.title: Ripasudil, KL001 and ABCA1 hypotheses for dry age-related macular degeneration
discoveries.ai_role: The Robin multi-agent system proposed drugs, requested analyses, interpreted returned results, and iterated its hypotheses.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers selected the problem, performed cell experiments and RNA sequencing, and checked AI analyses against human analyses.
discoveries.evidence_stage: in vitro validation in cell lines and geriatric primary human RPE cells
discoveries.novelty_scope: new repurposing and mechanism hypotheses
discoveries.reported_result: Ripasudil enhanced retinal-pigment-epithelium phagocytosis, KL001 was identified as a previously unproposed enhancer, and RNA-seq supported ABCA1 upregulation.
discoveries.caveat: The authors state that in vivo validation is still required; these are not validated treatments for dry AMD.

discoveries.title: LucaProt RNA-virus candidate atlas
discoveries.ai_role: A deep-learning model identified highly divergent RNA-dependent RNA polymerases in 10,487 metatranscriptomes.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers curated datasets, built phylogenies, and confirmed a subset with RT-PCR and RNA-versus-DNA sequencing.
discoveries.evidence_stage: published computational atlas with targeted molecular checks
discoveries.novelty_scope: putative new RNA-virus species and supergroups
discoveries.reported_result: The study reported 161,979 putative RNA-virus species across 180 supergroups; tens of thousands were described as previously unknown.
discoveries.caveat: These are sequence-defined putative species, not 161,979 isolated, cultured, or individually validated viruses.

discoveries.title: Contextual and combinatorial structure in sperm-whale codas
discoveries.ai_role: Machine-learning and statistical analyses modelled 8,719 codas from an Eastern Caribbean sperm-whale clan.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers collected and annotated recordings and interpreted the discovered acoustic features.
discoveries.novelty_scope: previously undescribed communication structure
discoveries.reported_result: The analysis identified rubato and ornamentation and showed that rhythm, tempo, rubato and ornamentation combine contextually, greatly expanding distinguishable coda patterns.
discoveries.caveat: The work did not translate whale language or establish the semantic meaning of codas, and it studied one social clan.

discoveries.title: Whole adult Drosophila brain connectome
discoveries.ai_role: Convolutional neural networks performed image alignment and initial neuron segmentation across electron-microscopy volumes.
discoveries.human_role: A large community manually proofread segmentation and assigned biological annotations, estimated at about 33 person-years of work.
discoveries.novelty_scope: first complete adult fly-brain wiring atlas at synaptic resolution
discoveries.reported_result: The atlas reconstructed 139,255 neurons and more than 50 million synapses, enabling circuit-wide biological analyses.
discoveries.caveat: This is a major AI-enabled map, not an autonomous AI discovery; proofreading and interpretation were deeply human.

discoveries.title: Higher-order like-to-like wiring rule in mouse visual cortex
discoveries.ai_role: AI-assisted functional modelling linked visual responses to a dense electron-microscopy connectome and tested wiring hypotheses.
discoveries.human_role: Researchers designed the experiments, imaged tissue and activity, reconstructed circuits, and interpreted connectivity statistics.
discoveries.novelty_scope: new organizing rule for neural connectivity
discoveries.reported_result: Beyond pairwise like-to-like connectivity, neurons sharing downstream targets were more functionally similar than pairwise rules predicted, revealing higher-order network structure.
discoveries.caveat: The result comes from a bounded mouse visual-cortex volume and should not be generalized to the whole brain or humans without further evidence.

exclusions.why_not_counted_as_a_strict_discovery: The objects had already been detected by the Kepler pipeline and existed as candidates; AI supplied statistical validation rather than first detection.
exclusions.revisit_condition: Include in a broader registry category for AI-enabled validation.

exclusions.claim_or_system: AlphaFold and the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database
exclusions.why_not_counted_as_a_strict_discovery: Predicted structures are scientifically useful but a prediction database is not itself a catalog of experimentally confirmed discoveries; individual downstream discoveries should be registered separately.
exclusions.revisit_condition: Add specific downstream biological discoveries when their empirical evidence and AI contribution are traceable.

exclusions.why_not_counted_as_a_strict_discovery: The campaign synthesized 36 of 57 targets, but later analysis and a correction highlighted prior or closely related compositions; counting all 36 as new materials would overstate novelty.
exclusions.revisit_condition: Reassess target by target against prior art and independent structural characterization.

exclusions.claim_or_system: Coscientist planned and executed cross-coupling reactions
exclusions.why_not_counted_as_a_strict_discovery: The demonstrated reactions and optimization tasks were known chemistry; the paper primarily established autonomous planning and execution capability.
exclusions.revisit_condition: Count only a later novel reaction, mechanism, or compound with explicit experimental novelty analysis.

exclusions.why_not_counted_as_a_strict_discovery: The system independently recapitulated a co-timed, then-unpublished human discovery; this is strong capability evidence but not a separate new scientific finding.
exclusions.revisit_condition: Represent in a dedicated rediscovery class if the registry expands beyond first discoveries.

exclusions.why_not_counted_as_a_strict_discovery: The work recovered many asteroid observations using an orbital-linking algorithm, but it is not clearly a learned AI system under this catalog's operational definition.
exclusions.revisit_condition: Include if the project adopts a broader definition covering all automated search and optimization algorithms.

exclusions.why_not_counted_as_a_strict_discovery: The primary paper describes automated bathymetric-depression detection, principal-component analysis, and expert classification, but does not establish a learned AI model; counting it would conflict with this catalog's operational definition.
exclusions.revisit_condition: Include if the project deliberately broadens scope from AI to computational automation.

exclusions.claim_or_system: Transformer-designed quantum experiments and state generalizations
exclusions.why_not_counted_as_a_strict_discovery: The system produced computational experiment designs and generalizations, but no corresponding laboratory discovery was established in the reviewed source.
exclusions.revisit_condition: Add to a separate theoretical/design tier or after physical realization.

exclusions.claim_or_system: Diagnostic classifiers, protein-property predictors, weather and climate forecasters
exclusions.why_not_counted_as_a_strict_discovery: Better prediction of a known label or future value is not a discovery unless the work also establishes a new object, mechanism, relationship, candidate, or law.
exclusions.revisit_condition: Evaluate individual studies when they make and validate a genuinely novel scientific claim.

coverage.what_was_covered: Exoplanets, radio transients, autonomous transient classification
coverage.main_gap_or_next_search: Systematic sweep of stellar, galactic, gravitational-wave, and cosmology literature.
Climate, oceanography, atmospheric chemistry, hydrology, mineralogy, and remote-sensing discoveries need dedicated reviews.
Broader satellite archaeology, paleoanthropology, and fossil-tomography literature needs systematic screening.

coverage.what_was_covered: Closed-loop formulation search, crystal prediction, generative material design
coverage.main_gap_or_next_search: Catalysis, reaction discovery, polymers, batteries, and contested autonomous-lab claims need target-by-target novelty audits.

coverage.review_status: seed audit strong but not exhaustive
coverage.main_gap_or_next_search: Cancer targets, rare disease, immunology, protein and peptide design, diagnostics, and later-stage replication need systematic expansion.
Gene regulation, microbiome, protein function, genome annotation, and synthetic biology remain under-covered.
Biodiversity surveys, conservation, species discovery, migration, and ecosystem mechanisms need dedicated review.
Human, vertebrate, molecular, cognitive, and clinical neuroscience remain under-covered.
